title: Intrinsic proper/open alpha horizontal equation on module sheaves
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For each scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the constant ring sheaf $\underline B_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $P_f$ for the specified inverse-image functor [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], $L_j$ for exact open extension [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension], and $\alpha(k,r,p,i;h):P_pL_i\to L_kP_r$ for the intrinsic ordinary clopen map [def-cbc-strict-tower-ordinary-proper-open-arrows]. The arrows in the following equations include the specified inverse-image compositors $c^P_{f,g}:P_{gf}\cong P_fP_g$, the unit-preserving open compositors $c^L_{i,j}:L_jL_i\cong L_{ji}$, and the cartesian open comparison $\beta$ [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization]. Let $k:A\hookrightarrow B_0$, $l:B_0\hookrightarrow E$, $i:C\hookrightarrow D$, and $j:D\hookrightarrow F$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $r:A\to C$, $p:B_0\to D$, and $q:E\to F$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $pk=ir$ and $ql=jp$. For every module sheaf $M$ on $C$ one has
$$\alpha(lk,r,q,ji)_M\circ P_q((c^L_{i,j})_M)=(c^L_{k,l})_{P_rM}\circ L_l(\alpha(k,r,p,i)_M)\circ\alpha(l,p,q,j)_{L_iM}.$$
This assertion is on module sheaves only.

proof.text: Restriction detects maps into open extension: transport module sheaves through fixedRestriction and fixedOpen, compose with the monomorphism openImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar, and use the restriction/direct-image adjunction. Naturality of fixedPull transports equality of module restrictions to equality of sheaf restrictions. Faithfulness of fixedRestriction gives equality of the original maps. This avoids the open/closed image argument.

Invert the unit-conjugation identity for the adjoint-defined open compositor. It says that restriction of the open compositor followed by the inverse composite unit equals the inverse-image compositor followed by the two successive inverse units.

Apply the single-square restriction identity to the outer square. Move the source open compositor past its inverse-image square by naturality and expand its inverse-unit composite by the previous step. The specified inverse-image square pasting identity rewrites the outer square comparison as the two successive square comparisons.

Expand the target open compositor by the inverse-unit composition identity. Move its inverse-image compositor past both alpha components using naturality. Naturality of the inverse open unit moves the first alpha through the second restricted extension. Apply the single-square restriction identity to both inner squares, then the first square comparison naturality to the remaining inverse open unit. The resulting word equals the outer restricted word. Cancel the invertible target inverse open unit and use restriction detection.

lean.statement:
theorem singleAlpha_horizontal {A C E B₀ D F : Scheme.{u}}
    (k : A ⟶ B₀) (l : B₀ ⟶ E) (i : C ⟶ D) (j : D ⟶ F)
    (r : A ⟶ C) (p : B₀ ⟶ D) (q : E ⟶ F)
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion l] [IsOpenImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact l] [QuasiCompact i] [QuasiCompact j]
    [IsProper r] [IsProper p] [IsProper q]
    (h₁ : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) (h₂ : l ≫ q = p ≫ j)
    (h : (k ≫ l) ≫ q = r ≫ (i ≫ j)) :
    ∀ M : Modules B C,
      (modulePullback B q).map ((openBetaModuleJComp B i j).hom.app M) ≫
          (singleAlpha B (k ≫ l) r q (i ≫ j) h).app M =
        (singleAlpha B l p q j h₂).app ((moduleJ B i).obj M) ≫
          (moduleJ B l).map ((singleAlpha B k r p i h₁).app M) ≫
          (openBetaModuleJComp B k l).hom.app ((modulePullback B r).obj M)
